Lumbar puncture. Assisting the doctor, step by step.

Step one. Know where to find the lumbar puncture policy, why the procedure is done, and your role as the nurse. Know the equipment, the safe holding technique, and the contraindications and complications.
Step two. Prepare the patient. Explain the procedure and make sure consent is taken. Organise the equipment, provide privacy, perform hand hygiene, and wear appropriate protective equipment.

Step three. Critical point. Position the patient on their side at the edge of the bed, with knees drawn up to the chest and chin tucked down, so the back curves outwards. Support the patient behind the neck and knees, and hold them safely throughout.
Step four. Critical point. Follow aseptic technique at every step. Keep the sterile field intact, assist the doctor as required, and keep watching the patient.
Step five. The doctor inserts the needle and stylet between the spinous processes, into the subarachnoid space. A free drip of cerebrospinal fluid confirms the position.
Step six. The spinal pressure may be measured with a manometer, attached to the needle by a three-way stopcock.
Step seven. The stopcock is then turned to collect the fluid into three to five sterile specimen tubes, in order. Note the colour and turbidity.

Step eight. After the needle is removed, apply gauze with tincture of iodine, and press directly on the site for thirty seconds. Apply an adhesive dressing. Dispose of the equipment, remove your gloves, and wash your hands.

Step nine. Critical point. After the procedure, observe the level of consciousness, pupil size and reaction, breathing, and vital signs. Ask about numbness, tingling, or pain down the legs, and check the site for swelling, bruising, or leaking fluid. Report any change promptly.
Step ten. Stay calm and reassuring, protect privacy with appropriate draping, communicate clearly with the team, and report any distress or complication.

Step eleven. Document the appearance of the fluid, the specimens sent, and the pressure readings. Record the patient's condition, vital signs, neurological status, and intake and output. Monitor the site, and if any adverse reaction occurs, record it and raise an O V A report.
Watch, take the quiz, then get signed off.
